items.title: e2e test paths vs. contract verifications as consumers grow
items.description: L2's comparison table says a full end-to-end test needs both services live, per test path. Without contract testing, every consumer needs its own set of end-to-end scenarios coordinated against a live provider — the number of paths grows with both the consumer count and how many scenarios each consumer needs checked. With contract testing, the provider runs one automated verification per consumer, regardless of how many scenarios that consumer's contract records, since it's all one fast local test run with no live coordination needed. Drag both sliders to see how far apart the two lines get.
items.compute: return { e2eTestPaths: params.consumers * params.scenariosPerConsumer, contractVerifications: params.consumers };

outputs.label: e2e test paths needed (no contract testing)

items.title: How often provider verification runs vs. how fast a breaking change is caught
items.description: Per L3's broker section, provider CI can run contract verification as often as every build. If verification only runs a few times a day, a breaking change can sit undetected for hours between runs; the closer verification gets to every build, the closer detection gets to immediate. This shows the worst case: a change that ships right after one verification run has to wait for the next one to be caught.

outputs.label: Worst-case days until a breaking change is caught
